seoTitle: How to Export Jotform to Google Sheets Automatically
metaDescription: Connect Jotform to Google Sheets with the native integration so form submissions sync to your spreadsheet in real time, no manual entry.
intro: Manually transferring form submissions into a spreadsheet slows down your workflow and increases the chance of errors. Jotform's native Google Sheets integration solves this by syncing every new response automatically. This guide walks through setting up the connection and mapping your form fields to spreadsheet columns.

steps.heading: Open the Integrations tab
steps.body: In your Jotform builder, navigate to Settings and find the Integrations tab.

steps.heading: Select the Google Sheets integration
steps.body: Choose the Google Sheets option from the list of available integrations.

steps.heading: Authenticate your Google account
steps.body: Log in and authorize your Google Workspace account to connect securely.

steps.heading: Choose or create a spreadsheet
steps.body: Decide whether to create a brand new spreadsheet or sync into an existing file.

steps.heading: Map form fields to columns
steps.body: Match your specific form questions to the corresponding spreadsheet columns.

steps.heading: Sync existing submissions and test
steps.body: Bring in past form entries automatically, then submit a live test to verify real-time syncing works.

faq.question: Will past submissions transfer over, or only new ones?
faq.answer: The integration is designed to sync existing submissions automatically in addition to capturing new ones going forward.

faq.question: Do I need to manually map every form field?
faq.answer: Yes, mapping your specific form questions to the correct spreadsheet columns is part of the setup process.

faq.question: Is the sync instant, or does it happen on a delay?
faq.answer: The integration is built for real-time syncing, so new submissions should appear in your spreadsheet shortly after being submitted.

faq.question: Can I use an existing spreadsheet instead of creating a new one?
faq.answer: Yes, during setup you can choose to sync into an existing Google Sheets file rather than starting from scratch.
